newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable after strengthening.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable after strengthening.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar after strengthening sharply earlier.

Dealers said the rise of the rupiah followed a surge in the ringgit against the U.S. currency after Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's warning of possible action against currency speculators.
"The surge of the ringgit spreaded to the rupiah quickly after a dull morning," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Mahathir said on Monday the government would consider taking punitive action against speculators. However, he did not outline what specific measures Malaysia might take.
"We were driven into the turbulence when the ringgit got hit last week. Now we are experiencing a recovery as the ringgit bounced back on verbal action," another dealer said.
Spot rupiah jumped to a high of 2,565 in early afternoon from 2,610 before settling at 2,585/95 at 0930 GMT. It opened at 2,605/15.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,581.5/87.5 and 2,604.0/09.0, respectively.
Trisiladi Supriyanto, vive president of Bank of America in Jakarta, said he expected the rupiah to gradually recover to the 2,550 level by the end of this week.
"Fund managers were already feeling comfortable with the rupiah and started to unload dollars, but they met resistance from local operators," Supriyanto said.
"The dollar would have adjusted lower if local operators had supported the downtrend momentum," he said.
Dealers said offshore operators sold the dollar down to 2,565 before domestic dollar purchases pushed the dollar back to the 2,590 level.
One local bank dealer said overnight dollars, however, rose to 13.0 percent from seven percent.
The U.S. bank dealer attributed the rise to technical factors rather than bullish dollar sentiment.
He said operators who arbitraged swaps with the money market were desperate for dollars to cover their positions.

The central bank had kept short-term money market rates high to reduce speculative dollar buying using cheap rupiah, but selective banks which had net open positions could arbitrage to gain attractive overnight rates of around 16.0/17.0 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.2/0.3 and tom/next at 0.20/0.25.
Overnight rupiah fluctuated between 14.0 and 17.0 percent throughout the day, with the last price quoted at 14.0 percent.
The central bank kept its interest rates for bilateral SBIs unchanged on Monday after raising the rates for one- and two-week papers by 200 basis points last Friday.

The bank offered one-to-three-day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent on Monday.
Bank Indonesia also scrapped purchase of short-term securities (SBPUs) on Monday to control excess rupiah.
Dealers said the central bank seemed to continue with its policy of gradually draining excess rupiah from the market.
They said swap rates were lower, in line with declining dollars in the spot market.
One-month swap fell to 17.0/20.0 from 21.0/23.0, two to 35.0/42.0 from 42.0/48.0, three to 54.0/60.0 from 63.0/73.0 and six to 113.0/117.0 from 125.0/135.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,571/2,619 on Monday from 2,592/2,640 on Friday.
